title: the Crescent Cove Rising Again
premise: Coral Thornbury, a cellist whose career shattered on stage three years ago, retreats to Crescent Cove to restore her grandmother's cottage and her nerve. There she discovers the anonymous pen pal who wrote her through her darkest decade is Jonah Reyes, the new neighbor and former coast guard officer who once testified against his own brother in a case that split their town. As Coral helps Jonah confront the town's lingering judgment, she must also face the truth that her final performance collapsed not from a faulty hand but from fear she never named. When a storm threatens the last ferry of the season and an old injustice resurfaces, Coral plays again — publicly, imperfectly, on her own terms — choosing both the cove and Jonah before winter closes the water.
about_author: Casper Pemberton is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who spent ten years writing letters to strangers across coastal towns. They now live somewhere foggy, where they collect ferry schedules and unfinished symphonies.

chapters.title: The Ferry That Almost Wasn't
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She arrives at Crescent Cove off-season, missing the last comfortable ferry by minutes and taking a fisherman's skiff instead. The cottage is colder than memory. Emotional beat: reluctant arrival, grief disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Letters in the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Restoring the cottage, she finds a tin of unsent letters addressed to 'the girl with the broken bow' — her own handwriting, never mailed. Emotional beat: shame resurfacing; the past has been waiting.

chapters.title: The Man Who Carries Wood Like an Apology
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He moves into the neighboring house, recognized instantly by half the hardware store. He chops wood for Coral unasked. Emotional beat: guarded kindness between two people fluent in exile.

chapters.title: A Cello in a Locked Room
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She uncovers her grandmother's cello under a dust sheet but cannot open the case. Flashback fragments of the catastrophic final performance intrude. Emotional beat: the body remembers what the mind refuses.

chapters.title: Coffee, Storm Warnings, and Other Small Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A shared generator during a blackout forces conversation; Jonah admits he knows her name from the news. Neither mentions his brother. Emotional beat: first real warmth, immediately armored over.

chapters.title: The Trial Everyone Remembers Wrongly
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the diner, old-timers relitigate the case that made him a pariah: he testified against his brother Danny for a harbor theft that drowned a man. Emotional beat: justice done, belonging lost.

chapters.title: Second Chances Are for People With Better Timing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A youth orchestra asks her to coach; she refuses at the door, then watches through glass. Jonah sees her watching. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by refusal.

chapters.title: What the Water Gave Back
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Divers recover Danny's old boat; evidence suggests someone else was aboard that night. Jonah's certainty cracks. Emotional beat: the vertigo of doubting your own testimony.

chapters.title: Duet, Unrehearsed
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Jonah finds her playing piano badly at midnight and joins in clumsily; laughter breaks something open. First kiss, interrupted by her panic. Emotional beat: joy arriving too fast to hold.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She finally opens the cello case and finds her grandmother's letter inside: forgiveness offered decades early. She cannot accept it yet. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a door, not a gift.

chapters.title: Danny Comes Home
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. His brother returns to the Cove, unrepentant or innocent — even he isn't sure anymore. Brothers meet in the rain and say nothing true. Emotional beat: love and suspicion wearing the same coat.

chapters.title: Rumors at the Lobster Pot
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Town gossip pairs her name with Jonah's disgrace; a concert patron from her past appears, offering a comeback tour if she distances herself. Emotional beat: temptation to be rescued rather than restored.

chapters.title: The Letter Writer Revealed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Coral discovers Jonah wrote her anonymous letters of encouragement after her disaster — he was the deckhand on the ferry that night, the only stranger who stayed. Emotional beat: betrayal and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: Why You Never Signed Your Name
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He explains: guilt. He watched her collapse and did nothing, then wrote letters as penance. Coral feels like a charity case. Emotional beat: the wound of being loved out of obligation.

chapters.title: Cold Harbor, Cold Shoulder
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She withdraws; the youth orchestra rehearses without her; the cottage goes silent again. Jonah stops chopping wood. Emotional beat: the familiar fortress rebuilt, lonelier than before.

chapters.title: The Witness Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. New evidence surfaces: a third man on Danny's boat, connected to the harbormaster who prosecuted the case. Justice outside the law becomes necessary. Emotional beat: righteous anger finding its spine.

chapters.title: Storm Front Over Crescent Cove
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The season's last ferry approaches ahead of a gale; the harbormaster moves to destroy the recovered evidence. Jonah and Danny, uneasy allies, race the tide. Emotional beat: brothers fighting for the same truth.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the dock, Coral must choose: board the ferry to the tour and the old life, or stay. She sees Jonah handcuffed briefly in the melee, protecting the evidence. Emotional beat: the decision point of the whole book.

chapters.title: What She Played Instead
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She doesn't board. Instead she carries her grandmother's cello to the dock shelter and plays — badly at first, then honestly — while the storm rages and the town listens. Emotional beat: public vulnerability as triumph.

chapters.title: Testimony in D Minor
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The performance draws the crowd that forces the harbormaster's cover-up into daylight; Danny is cleared. Jonah, cleared of nothing, forgives himself anyway. Emotional beat: justice and mercy arriving separately.

chapters.title: Forgiveness Is a Door You Walk Through Twice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She mails the unsent letters at last, then writes one new one — signed — and leaves it on Jonah's porch. Winter light, open windows. Emotional beat: forgiving herself by finishing what she started.

chapters.title: Spring Comes Early to the Cove
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later: Coral coaches the youth orchestra, Jonah rebuilds the dock, and the two play duets on Sundays. The ferry runs year-round now. Emotional beat: belonging chosen daily, not granted once.
